text.p: SpectraLink Corp said Wednesday it is confident revenues will top $50 million in fiscal 1998 spurred by lower prices and a larger sales force.

Revenues in fiscal 1997 should grow to about $31 million compared with revenues of $21.5 million in 1996 while earnings per share should be about $0.08, below the $0.14 a share in the previous year, Chief Financial Officer Bill Mansfield told Reuters at the Hambrecht & Quist technology conference here.
Mansfield said he is confident revenues in fiscal 1998 will jump to above $50 million with earnings of about $0.45 a share.

Behind the revenue growth is a doubling of the sales force which the company implemented in the first quarter of 1997, Mansfield said. In the first quarter the company lost $0.03 a share pirmarily because of the costs associated with increasing the sales force.

Another factor driving revenues higher is lower costs, Mansfield said. Total costs per unit for the company's flagship S400 product, a handheld wireless phone for use within a business, has dropped to about $850 from $1,200, he said.

In April the company received its biggest ever order. The $1.7 million order was for K-Mart which equipped about 100 of its superstores with SpectraLink's wireless phones. Growth in 1997 will be driven by the retail sector with an increase in sales to hospitals expected in th fourth quarter, Mansfield said.
